blocks.b99:
*The young woman with the Quest tags looks up first—then the grey-haired man lifts a hand and she goes back to her sorting.*

"Registration's over here with me." *He turns the register sideways on the counter, unhurried.* "Name?"

*He's already pulling a fresh sheet of paper toward himself, dipping a nib. The inkwell leaves a dark ring on the worn wood. Up close he smells of pipe smoke and stamp ink, and his eyes do a quick, practised pass over Alaric—the sword, the armor, the hands.*

"Fair warning on how this runs. Name, age, whether you can read and write. Then you press blood to the sheet—a pin prick, nothing worse—and the Guild stone confirms your Rank. Whole thing takes a quarter hour." *He sets a fat iron pin on the counter beside the register, its point fine as a needle.* "There's the matter of the fee. Two silver for a Novice's medallion and entry in the rolls. Paid once, yours for life, every branch honors it."

*He glances at the sword again, then back to the blank line on the page.*

"Two silver, and I write your name down. That's the whole bargain. So—name and age, and we'll begin."

*Behind him the woman with the tags calls out a Quest number to a waiting pair of hunters; a bench scrapes somewhere in the hall's depths. The counter between them holds the pen, the pin, the open page—everything waiting on him.*

*The clerk takes the two silver coins off the counter with a swipe of his thumb, bites one out of old habit, and drops both into a locked drawer beneath the register.*

"Alaric Red. Eighteen. Letters." *The nib scratches it all down in a cramped, quick hand.* "Word of advice—hold the pin like you mean it. First-timers flinch and I have to blot the page."

*Alaric doesn't flinch. The pin's point bites the pad of his finger, a sting no deeper than a nettle, and dark drops fall onto the sheet. The clerk watches the blood soak into the paper with mild approval.*

"Steady hands. Good."

*He turns the register to face a squat block of grey stone set into the counter's end, worn smooth where thousands of palms have rested before. Alaric puts his hand on it. The stone is cool at first, then warms under his palm—a slow pulse, like something with a heartbeat turning over in its sleep. A faint line of light travels the length of the block and dies.*

"Rank F," *the clerk reads off the surface, unsurprised.* "Novice. Everyone starts there. Warrior's build on you, but the stone doesn't care what I think."

*He stamps the page, blows on the ink, and reaches under the counter. What comes out is a wooden case, and inside it a medallion—a dull iron disc stamped with the crossed sword and arrow, a fresh F scored beneath. He slides the case across.*

"Rules you'll actually use: medallion stays on you inside Guild halls. Quests come off that board there, Novice-tagged only until you rank up. Complete them at the counter, get paid here, same counter. Abandon a Quest you've taken twice and we'll have a different conversation." *He's already turning the register back around for the next name.* "Congratulations and welcome to the Guild, Alaric Red. Counter's this end for payouts, Hessa's end for Quest tags."

*The young woman down the counter—Hessa, presumably—doesn't look up from her sorting.*

*The notice board stands chest-high, a frame of oak crowded with sheets of varying age. The newest ones sit at eye level, each tagged with a wooden chip stamped F in white paint. Ink has faded on the older postings; one corner sheet is so sun-bleached its words have gone ghost-grey.*

*The Novice-tagged selection, this morning:*

**WOLF PROBLEM — MILLBROOK HAMLET.** Sheep kills over the past week, likely a small pack out of the eastern woods. Hamlet will guide to the last kill site. Pay: 8 silver on proof of at least two wolves. Novice.

**HERB RUN — damp hollows south of the river.** Gatheror wants fresh marshmallow root and yarrow, ten bundles each, before the week is out. Roots, not blades. Pay: 4 silver. Novice.

**CART GUARD — ALDERWATCH TO FERRY CROSSING.** Wool merchant needs a spear or sword on the bench, two days out, one day back. Departure tomorrow at dawn. Pay: 6 silver plus a meal. Novice.

**RATS IN THE GRAIN CELLARS.** The tally-house on Chandler Street wants cellars cleared. Bring proof—tails. Pay: 3 silver. Novice. *Someone has written beneath it, in a different hand: "bring a lantern and no pride."*

**LOST DOG — reward posted by name, Marta Hale.** Brown bitch, one crooked ear, answers to Pip. Last seen by the south gate. Pay: 1 silver. Novice.

*Wooden tags hang from nails beside each sheet. Take the tag, take the Quest.*

*Around him the hall goes on with its morning: the two hunters at the map table have stopped arguing and started rolling the map up; someone laughs near the hearth; the whetstone keeps its slow rhythm. Hessa's sorting has ended—she's now facing the board's end of the counter, arms crossed, watching the room with the patience of someone paid by the hour.*

blocks.b109:
*Hessa takes the wolf tag off its nail, copies the Quest number into a register, and stamps the sheet against Alaric's medallion without ceremony.*

"Proof's two carcasses or pelts. Counter's this end when you're back. Don't drag them through the front door bloody."

*The eastern road leaves Alderwatch through the wool gate, past pens and bleating, then runs between hedgerows and turnip fields. It's a good three hours on foot. Cart traffic thins after the second mile; a raven follows the ditch for a while, then gives up on him. By late morning the land starts to lift into wooded ridges, and the road dips toward a stream where a hamlet sits—two dozen buildings, a mill with its wheel turning, sheep pens on the near side.*

*The pens are the thing everyone's talking about. A knot of villagers stands at the fence, and the smell carries before the sight: blood and opened wool. One ewe dead in the trampled grass, another gone entirely, and an old dog pacing the fence line with its hackles up.*

*A broad man with a miller's dust still on his forearms sees the sword and the medallion and comes down the lane to meet him, wiping his hands on his apron.*

"Guild, then? For the wolves?" *He looks Alaric over—armor, youth, the F stamped on the iron—and his mouth pulls sideways, but he doesn't say what he's thinking.* "Tomas. I run the mill. Third kill this week, and my neighbor's lost five. Happens at night, always at night. We found this one at dawn."

*He turns and points up the slope behind the pens, toward a dark line of trees.*

"Sheep trail runs up through the alders to where it happened. I'll walk you to the kill site if you're ready now—sheep don't wait on anybody's schedule. You want to see it before the rain comes in and takes the sign."

*Overhead the sky has gone a flat, heavy white. The dog at the fence has stopped pacing and is watching the tree line.*

blocks.b112:
MONSTER ECOLOGY / FAUNA [CANON]
Native non-sapient fauna are part of Avereth's Monster ecology. Familiar animal-shaped creatures such as wolves, deer, horses, boars, bears and birds are mechanically Monsters with Level and Rank even when peaceful, domesticated or ecologically ordinary. 'Animal' remains normal everyday language for ecology/body type; it is not a separate rules category.

Monster classification does NOT mean hostility. Monsters are natural populations: they reproduce, compete, migrate, form territories/social structures, are hunted or domesticated, and may evolve through Ranks. Most ordinary fauna near settlements are F-rank; evolved higher-rank specimens become progressively rarer and more dangerous.

Sapience is separate from Monster classification. Some Monsters speak, organize societies, rule territory and conduct diplomacy.
VALEDORN CROWN [CANON + REGIONAL SEED]
Position: central Avereth. Capital: Crownheart. Strongest human kingdom. Public S-ranks: 3.

Valedorn is a political center of human diplomacy with deep noble lineages, wealthy academies, old military institutions and one of the largest Adventurers' Guild headquarters. Its strength is breadth: population, wealth, administration, magic, military organization and diplomacy rather than one narrow specialty.

GENERATION FLAVOR: portray layered institutions, patronage, old rights, busy roads, provincial differences and court influence without making every scene court politics. Wealth and sophistication coexist with ordinary villages and practical local problems. Valedorn is powerful but coalitions can constrain it.
AVERETH — CANON AND GENERATIVE SPACE [AUTHORING RULE]
This lorebook is narrator/world knowledge, not knowledge any NPC automatically has. Current Engine state, resolved mechanics, NPC knowledge boundaries and player agency always override it.

Blank space is intentional. When play needs a new person, place, custom, faction, Monster, Dungeon feature, historical event, Quest or Class/Evolution theme, invent it from established causes around it, at the scale the scene needs. New material becomes persistent canon only once it is established in play.
AVERETH — WORLD IDENTITY [CANON]
The known world is dominated by one immense continent, Avereth, surrounded by ocean. Recorded history is extremely deep: civilizations, dynasties, religions and peoples have risen and vanished, and a few ancient beings remember eras ordinary people know only as legend.

The tone is high fantasy with contrast. Safe cities, farms, workshops, trade, families, festivals and ordinary careers coexist with dangerous wilderness, Monsters, natural Dungeons, political violence and ancient powers. The world is not uniformly grim and is not built as a sequence of combat zones.

Current established great powers are six human kingdoms — Valedorn Crown, Caelreth, Veyrhold, Solmere, Ilyrion and Duskreach — plus two recognized monster realms, the Ashen Scale Dominion and Verdant Fang Court. Human and monster states are not unified species blocs; trade, diplomacy, rivalry, war and cooperation can cross species lines.

Material culture is Western-fantasy medieval alongside mana and high magic. Modern or industrial technology is not the default.
blocks.b113:
*Tomas grabs a crook-handled walking stick from beside his door and leads him up the sheep trail. The alders close in overhead, wet leaves slapping at their shoulders, and the pen noise falls away behind them. Twenty minutes up the slope he stops and points with the stick.*

"Here. This is where we found the ewe."

*The site is a churned mess of mud and wool. Tomas hangs back by a tree, arms folded, saying nothing more—he said he'd bring him, and he's a man who keeps to what he said.*

*The ground tells its story plainly. Two sets of paw prints pressed deep, hind claws dug in where they braced to drag. Drag marks in the mud run uphill, north-by-northeast, with tufts of bloody wool snagged on the bracken every few strides. The prints are broad-padded, one animal noticeably larger than the other. Scat near the trail edge, still soft—a day old at most, fur in it. They fed here or near here, then pulled the carcass higher up, into the deeper wood where the alders give way to dark pine.*

*Rain patters down through the canopy, fat first drops, and the prints are already beginning to soften at the edges. Whatever the pack is, it's denned or resting north of here, likely no more than a couple miles off. Given the depth of the sign and the size of the bigger animal, these are no starving strays—they're working wolves, and there's at least one big bitch or dog leading them.*

*Tomas shifts his weight against the tree.* "Well? You read anything off it?"

blocks.b117:
*Tomas doesn't argue. He looks at the trees, then at the boy with the sword, and nods once.*

"Suit yourself. I'll tell the others the Guild's on it. If you're not back by dark we'll come looking—maybe." *He turns and starts down the trail, stick tapping on stone, and is gone below the alders within a minute.*

*The rain settles in properly after that, a steady hiss through the leaves. The trail is easy to hold—drag marks, wool, the deep prints—climbing through alder into pine, where the light goes grey-green and the needle floor swallows the mud but not the story: a smeared blood streak on a root, a scuffed patch where the carcass was set down and dragged again.*

*Maybe a mile and a half north the wood changes character. Bones under a deadfall—sheep, older, gnawed pale. More scat. And then, on a slope looking down into a shallow ravine with a dark hollow at its base, the smell hits: musk, rank wet fur, old kills.*

*Two wolves are in the ravine. One is dozing, flank twitching, ears flat—a yearling by its size. The other stands at the hollow's mouth, head up, rain dripping off its jaw. It's a big bitch, deep-chested, a fresh nick across her muzzle. She isn't looking upslope yet, but her nose works the air, and the wind has been drifting downhill from Alaric's side of the ridge.*

*She takes one step out of the hollow, tests the air again, and holds still.*

LOOT / MATERIAL GENERATION BODY [CREATIVE SCAFFOLD]
External loot should have a source and physical existence. For a new material/item establish only what is needed:
SOURCE — corpse, plant, mineral, workshop, cache, Dungeon, owner.
FORM — what can physically be carried/harvested.
USE — craft, food, alchemy, ritual, trade, tool, trophy, etc.
MARKET — who values it and why.
RARITY — local abundance versus scarcity.
OWNERSHIP/RISK — whether taking it is lawful, contested or dangerous.

Do not auto-pick up, harvest, sell or convert objects into Coin. Generic Gear does not acquire a legendary maker, hidden faction mark or ancient provenance without a real cause.
VALEDORN CROWN [CANON + REGIONAL SEED]
Position: central Avereth. Capital: Crownheart. Strongest human kingdom. Public S-ranks: 3.

Valedorn is a political center of human diplomacy with deep noble lineages, wealthy academies, old military institutions and one of the largest Adventurers' Guild headquarters. Its strength is breadth: population, wealth, administration, magic, military organization and diplomacy rather than one narrow specialty.

GENERATION FLAVOR: portray layered institutions, patronage, old rights, busy roads, provincial differences and court influence without making every scene court politics. Wealth and sophistication coexist with ordinary villages and practical local problems. Valedorn is powerful but coalitions can constrain it.
AVERETH — CANON AND GENERATIVE SPACE [AUTHORING RULE]
This lorebook is narrator/world knowledge, not knowledge any NPC automatically has. Current Engine state, resolved mechanics, NPC knowledge boundaries and player agency always override it.

Blank space is intentional. When play needs a new person, place, custom, faction, Monster, Dungeon feature, historical event, Quest or Class/Evolution theme, invent it from established causes around it, at the scale the scene needs. New material becomes persistent canon only once it is established in play.
AVERETH — WORLD IDENTITY [CANON]
The known world is dominated by one immense continent, Avereth, surrounded by ocean. Recorded history is extremely deep: civilizations, dynasties, religions and peoples have risen and vanished, and a few ancient beings remember eras ordinary people know only as legend.

The tone is high fantasy with contrast. Safe cities, farms, workshops, trade, families, festivals and ordinary careers coexist with dangerous wilderness, Monsters, natural Dungeons, political violence and ancient powers. The world is not uniformly grim and is not built as a sequence of combat zones.

Current established great powers are six human kingdoms — Valedorn Crown, Caelreth, Veyrhold, Solmere, Ilyrion and Duskreach — plus two recognized monster realms, the Ashen Scale Dominion and Verdant Fang Court. Human and monster states are not unified species blocs; trade, diplomacy, rivalry, war and cooperation can cross species lines.

Material culture is Western-fantasy medieval alongside mana and high magic. Modern or industrial technology is not the default.
blocks.b121:
*Steel scrapes free of the scabbard and the sound carries down the ravine like a thrown stone.*

*The yearling's head snaps up, sleep gone. The bitch drops into a crouch in the same heartbeat—no hesitation, no test of nerve. Her lip peels off yellowed teeth and a growl rolls up the slope, low and even, the sound of an animal that has killed before and expects to again. She doesn't run. She comes out of the hollow at a lope, angled, flanking toward the ridge—using the ground, cutting the slope between Alaric and the open pine—and the yearling boils up out of the ravine behind her, younger, noisier, yelping as it scrambles over a deadfall.*

*Rain on the needles. Rain on Alaric's shoulders. The bitch closes the distance in long, eating strides, ears pinned, her wounded muzzle wrinkled, and the moment her haunches bunch the thing is no longer a standoff at all—*
blocks.b122: *i Heavy Slash the Pack Leader Bitch*
blocks.b123:
*The yearling reaches him first—low, fast, teeth closing on his forearm above the bracer. Pain flares hot and shallow, and then the bitch is there, hitting his thigh like a thrown sack of grain, jaws punching through cloth into muscle. He staggers under the doubled weight of two bodies wrenching in opposite directions.*

*He wrenches the sword free of the yearling's grip and swings it down in one heavy, committed arc into the bitch's neck. The blade goes deep. Her jaws tear loose as she falls, taking a mouthful of trouser and flesh with her, and she rolls sideways down the slope, kicks twice against a root, and goes still. Rain fills the open red line across her back.*

*The yearling lunges again while his arm is still coming up—teeth raking his shoulder, a shallow rip through armor leather—and then it leaps back a stride, hackles up, circling onto the pine needles between him and the ravine. Its eyes flick to the bitch's body, back to him, and it yelps once, high and cracked, pawing the ground.*

*Blood runs warm down Alaric's forearm and thigh, thinned by rain. The yearling's haunches coil. It is still coming.*
blocks.b124: *I Heavy Slash the Yearling Wolf A*
blocks.b125:
*It comes in low and fast, the same line as before—and Alaric is already swinging. The blade catches it mid-leap, across the shoulder and through the ribs, and the yearling's yelp cuts off into a wet, coughing sound. It hits the needles at his feet, legs scrabbling once against a root, and then it stops moving. Rain beads on its grey flank.*

*Then there is only rain. Rain on pine, rain running off his blade and dripping pink into the needles, rain filling the tracks the wolves churned into the slope.*

*Alaric's forearm bleeds steadily where the yearling's teeth went in above the bracer—shallow, ugly, a tooth-marked crescent. His thigh burns where the bitch's jaws punched through trouser and skin, and his shoulder carries a long rake through armor leather that has opened the skin beneath. Nothing is broken. He can stand, and he can walk, but every step sends a dull throb through the leg.*

*The bitch lies rolled against a root a few yards downhill, her neck at a wrong angle, rain pooling red in the fur beneath her. The hollow at the ravine's base is dark and silent. No more shapes come out of it. Whatever else the pack was, it isn't here.*

*Two wolves. Two bodies. Proof for Millbrook, eight silver, if he can carry it back.*
blocks.b126: *I butcher the Wolves to loot them and take that loot as Proof. I then walk back to Millbrook*

blocks.b128:
*The bitch first. Kneeling costs his thigh a protest, a hot pull with every shift of weight, but the work itself is simple and ugly. The starter blade is sharper than it has any right to be for the price; it parts hide and sinew in rough strokes, and rain keeps washing the blood off his hands faster than he can wipe them. He takes the head at the neck joints, sawing through gristle until the spine grinds apart, and does the same for the yearling where it lies. Two heads, heavy and wet, tongues lolling, eyes already glazing with rain in them. Proof enough for any hamlet that has been losing sheep.*

*He wraps them in a square of canvas cut from the yearling's bedding ground—pine boughs and a scrap of oiled cloth from his pack—and ties the bundle to his belt hook. The rest he leaves to the crows and the ravine. By the time he straightens, his knee is stiff with cold and his forearm has glued itself to the bracer in a tacky film of blood.*

*The walk down is slow. The pine needles give way to bracken and then to the trampled mud of the kill site, and from there the hamlet's guides' path is easy to find even in the rain. Forty minutes of it, downhill, bundle swinging at his hip, leg throbbing in time with his steps.*

*Millbrook comes up out of the grey in ones and twos: slate roofs, smoke bending from chimneys, a dog barking itself hoarse behind a fence. Two women under an eave see him first—the bundle, then the blood—and one pulls the other back a step. A boy goes running up the lane, shouting something toward the alehouse.*

*By the time Alaric reaches the well at the lane's center, a thickset man in a wet shepherd's cloak is already striding toward him, squinting at what hangs at his hip.*

"That's—" He stops an arm's length off, rain dripping off his hood. "That's the big one. The black-eared bitch." He looks up, and there's something between relief and disbelief in his face. "You went up there alone?"

blocks.b131:
*The heads thump onto the wet cobbles by the well, canvas unwinding. The shepherd takes a half-step back, then leans in again, crouching to look. His calloused hand hovers over the black-eared skull without touching it.*

"That's her, all right." He looks up. "And the other?"

"Yearling," one of the women under the eaves calls. "Grey, isn't it? That's the one that took the Hollis lamb Tuesday."

The shepherd straightens, wiping rain off his chin. "Aye. That'll do." He squints at Alaric, at the medallion chain just visible at his collar, then at the blood caking his forearm. "You want it written. Right. Only I don't hold a pen worth spit, and neither does most here." He jerks a thumb back up the lane, toward a longhouse with a lantern already lit in its window despite the hour. "Reeve Aldous does the hamlet's tallying. He'll mark your paper—count the heads as proof, put his name to it. That's all you'll want, I'd take it."

He glances at the heads again, then back up. "You'll want that arm looked at too, before it turns bad. Marta boils her needles for stitching." A pause, and something less businesslike enters his voice. "Eight silver, is what the reeve posted? He'll grumble at the coin, but he'll pay it. He's honest, Aldous. Grumbling's free."

Somewhere down the lane, the dog is still barking. The boy who ran ahead is talking fast to a knot of three men outside the alehouse, gesturing toward the well, and one of them starts walking over.

CURRENCY / EVERYDAY ECONOMY [CANON]
Common currency uses whole coins: 10 Copper = 1 Silver; 10 Silver = 1 Gold. There is no standard fractional Copper.

Prices are intentionally contextual rather than globally fixed. Cost should reflect local supply, demand, danger, transport, quality, scarcity, law and bargaining position. Legal trade can include food, lodging, transport, tools, Gear, magical services, Skill Stones, Monster/Dungeon materials, healing, training, maps and information.

Wealth is uneven. A valuable reward should come from a giver who can plausibly afford it or from property/resources that actually exist. Do not inflate every adventuring job into treasure-scale economics.
GUILD CONTRACT BOARDS [CANON]
Every active branch keeps AT LEAST FIVE currently available contracts for each Guild Rank it supports. Small branches need not support every Rank; higher-rank work can arrive through regional or transnational Guild networks instead of five local Master or Legend crises.

The board changes once per in-world day, never as a full reroll: still-valid unresolved contracts stay; taken, completed, expired or withdrawn ones leave; new ones restore the minimum. Other adventurers take work, so an ignored contract can vanish, change or be resolved without Alaric. Listings Alaric has already seen stay the same until they change for such a reason.

Listings show the Quest Rank, never a Recommended Level. When Alaric reads a board, describe only the listings at his own Guild Rank (a glance at the rest at most) instead of reciting every Rank; most listings are routine standing work.
REDMARCH [CANON SEED]
A walled city in Veyrhold and a possible campaign starting city. Exact local details remain open.

GENERATION DIRECTION: make fortification, military traffic, hunting expertise or frontier logistics visible without turning the whole city into a barracks. Local economy and current border pressures should be established only when relevant.
VEYRHOLD [CANON + REGIONAL SEED]
Position: eastern Avereth. Capital: Ironward. Top-tier martial kingdom. Public S-ranks: 2.

Veyrhold is heavily militarized and shaped by dangerous borders. Martial training, disciplined officer corps, fortified cities and Monster-hunting traditions are central. Its most openly tense great-power relationship is with the Ashen Scale Dominion, though both avoid escalation into direct S-rank war.

GENERATION FLAVOR: fortification, logistics, readiness, veteran culture, border economies and social weight of service. Military presence should vary by location; civilians still trade, farm, marry, argue and live ordinary lives.
AVERETH — CANON AND GENERATIVE SPACE [AUTHORING RULE]
This lorebook is narrator/world knowledge, not knowledge any NPC automatically has. Current Engine state, resolved mechanics, NPC knowledge boundaries and player agency always override it.

Blank space is intentional. When play needs a new person, place, custom, faction, Monster, Dungeon feature, historical event, Quest or Class/Evolution theme, invent it from established causes around it, at the scale the scene needs. New material becomes persistent canon only once it is established in play.
AVERETH — WORLD IDENTITY [CANON]
The known world is dominated by one immense continent, Avereth, surrounded by ocean. Recorded history is extremely deep: civilizations, dynasties, religions and peoples have risen and vanished, and a few ancient beings remember eras ordinary people know only as legend.

The tone is high fantasy with contrast. Safe cities, farms, workshops, trade, families, festivals and ordinary careers coexist with dangerous wilderness, Monsters, natural Dungeons, political violence and ancient powers. The world is not uniformly grim and is not built as a sequence of combat zones.

Current established great powers are six human kingdoms — Valedorn Crown, Caelreth, Veyrhold, Solmere, Ilyrion and Duskreach — plus two recognized monster realms, the Ashen Scale Dominion and Verdant Fang Court. Human and monster states are not unified species blocs; trade, diplomacy, rivalry, war and cooperation can cross species lines.

Material culture is Western-fantasy medieval alongside mana and high magic. Modern or industrial technology is not the default.

The road takes him in through the western gate with a trickle of carts and foot traffic. A guard in Veyrhold grey glances at the rapier on his hip, finds nothing worth a question in it, and waves him on with the rest. Beyond the gate the street narrows between timber-framed buildings — a farrier's hammer ringing somewhere to the left, the smell of hot iron and wet straw, a woman arguing with a fishmonger about the smell of his stall.

He passes a notice board plastered with levy notices and grain prices, follows a painted sign — crossed swords over a huntsman's horn — down a side lane, and the Guildhall stands at the end of it: older stone than its neighbors, a wide door propped open to the morning.

Inside, the noise changes. Boots on flagstone, the scrape of a whetstone, low talk around long tables. A hearth burns at one end; a wall of wooden Quest slips lines the other, ranks marked in painted bands. A few heads turn as he enters — the natural, brief assessment strangers get in a border town — then go back to their breakfasts.

A long counter runs along the right side. Behind it stands a woman in her thirties with close-cropped brown hair and a Guild tabard over a mail shirt, sorting slips into a pigeonhole rack. She clocks him as he crosses the threshold, takes in the sword, the clothes, the lack of any Guild mark.

"Morning." She sets down the stack of slips. "Looking to post something, take something, or register?"

GUILD QUEST RANK CALIBRATION [GENERATION SCAFFOLD]

Guild Quest Rank is an institutional assessment of the responsibility, danger, uncertainty and expected capability of a contract:
NOVICE — routine local work, low institutional risk, ordinary early-career contracts.
PROVEN — established professional work with meaningful danger, uncertainty or responsibility.
VETERAN — serious professional assignments where reliable independent judgment is expected.
ELITE — high-risk or high-consequence contracts requiring exceptional competence.
MASTER — Half-Divine/B-rank-scale institutional work; rare and regionally significant.
GRANDMASTER — A-rank-scale strategic contracts; very rare and usually regional/international.
LEGEND — S-rank-scale strategic matters; exceptional, not ordinary local board filler.

Quest Rank belongs to the Guild's contract system. It does NOT alter the actual world to match the adventurer, and a listed Quest may prove easier, harder or differently complicated than expected because Guild information can be incomplete.

Do not use a public "Recommended Level" field in Guild presentation. The person's Power Rank and Guild Rank remain separate from Quest Rank.

QUEST GENERATION — CAUSAL RULE [GENERATION SCAFFOLD]
A Quest is not content vending. It begins because someone or some institution wants the world to be different from how it is now.

Before generating a Quest, establish:
CAUSE — what current condition created the need?
STAKEHOLDER — who cares, and why?
KNOWLEDGE — how does the giver know there is a problem?
CAPABILITY GAP — why does the giver need outside help?
DESIRED STATE — what would count as success?
MEANS — what reward, authority, information or access can the giver realistically provide?

Generate Quests from existing people, places, shortages, threats, obligations, trade, politics, ecology, previous outcomes and newly established local conditions. Do not manufacture a crisis simply because Alaric is present.

GUILD BOARD MINIMUMS do not mean every new listing must be a fresh emergency. A branch can maintain its required pool through routine standing work, escorts, surveys, deliveries, material procurement, pest control, training support, investigation, repair/security work and regional-network contracts. The board should feel economically and institutionally plausible rather than like five catastrophes per Rank per day.
COMPLETE QUEST BODY [GENERATION SCAFFOLD]
When a new tracked Quest is actually offered, silently ensure it has:

1. TITLE — practical and locally meaningful.
2. GIVER — a real person/institution with authority or stake.
3. CAUSE — the existing problem/opportunity.
4. MOTIVE — why the giver cares.
5. DESIRED END STATE — what completion means.
6. QUEST RANK — for Guild contracts: Novice / Proven / Veteran / Elite / Master / Grandmaster / Legend. Private work has no Quest Rank unless the Guild lists it.
7. OBJECTIVE PATH — normally 1-4 meaningful steps; more only when fiction supports it.
8. ACCESS/KNOWLEDGE — what the player is told and what remains unknown.
9. COMPLETION EVIDENCE — how the giver can know the task is done; for a Guild contract, the proof Alaric brings to a Guild front desk (trophies, a signed or sealed confirmation, a receipt).
10. REWARD SOURCE — why the reward exists and who can provide it; for a Guild contract, one fixed payout the client deposits with the Guild, which pays it at the turn-in (per-unit or discretionary extras are a separate client bonus).
11. CONSEQUENCE — what changes on success, failure, refusal or delay when relevant.

Do not pre-author every branch. Let branches emerge from player decisions and changing world state.

"Registration." She nods, already reaching under the counter. "Name?"

Whatever he answers, she scratches it onto a fresh form in a quick, practiced hand. "Right. Redmarch branch, so this goes in the Veyrhold rolls. Rules are short: you start Novice rank, you take Novice contracts, you don't take work above your rank without a waiver from a desk clerk. Contracts pay as posted. Falsifying a completion gets you expelled, and in a border town we do check."

She produces a palm-sized sphere of cloudy grey crystal from a drawer and sets it on the counter between them.

"Hand on this. It reads Rank and general condition — nothing else, and it doesn't hurt. It's how we keep the Novice board honest."

While she waits, she pulls a second slip toward her. "Registration fee is two silver, one-time. That covers your plate, your first stamp, and board access. After that the Guild takes a cut of contract payouts, not out of your pocket." She glances up at him, pen poised. "So — two silver and a hand on the stone, and you're in the book. Questions first, if you have them."

blocks.b144:
The clerk counts the two silver, stamps the form, and slides a wooden plate across the counter — fresh-cut, his name burned into it in the same quick hand, a Novice stamp in the corner still wet.

"Press when you're ready."

The crystal is cool under his palm. Clouds turn inside it, slow, then settle into a flat grey. "F-rank, condition's clean," she says, reading it the way a farrier reads a hoof. "Fine. Board's on the far wall, Novice band's the bottom row in blue. Take a slip, bring it back here and I'll log it under your name."

The plate goes into his hand; she's already back to her pigeonholes before he turns away.

The Novice band holds a dozen slips. Most are the standing sort — wood-hauling for the palisade works, night watch at the east granary, rat-clearing in the tannery cellars at four copper a head. Five are pinned newer, ink still dark:

**Miller's Run Escort** — Cart of flour to the waystation on the south road. Two days' there and back. Novice. 8 silver.

**Weasel Sign at Fenwick's Coop** — Something small and toothy has been in the henhouses three nights running. Find it, kill it, bring the pelt. Novice. 15 silver.

**Herb Run — Marshmint** — Gather a full basket of marshmint from the reedbeds east of the mill leat. Wet work. Novice. 4 silver.

**Missing Dog, Tanner's Row** — Brown bitch, lame left foreleg, gone since the market day. Find and return. Novice. 2 silver.

**Fence Repair, Widow Marsh** — Beast-broken palings on the north paddock. Hammer and nails provided. Novice. 5 silver.

Two adventurers in mud-caked boots stand at the board; one pulls the weasel slip off its nail without looking at anyone and carries it to the counter.

The clerk takes the slip, checks the nail it came from against her rack, and writes his name into a register beside it.

"Miller's Run. Cart leaves from the miller's yard — Grainmarket Row, the big yard behind Harrow's mill — tomorrow at first light. You'll be walking beside the carter, Ossler, and one other Novice took the second escort slot last evening, so you won't be alone if anything four-legged takes an interest in the flour." She stamps the slip. "Waystation master signs your plate at delivery. Bring it back here for payout — eight silver."

She slides the stamped slip across the counter. "Anything above F shows up on that road now and then, so keep your eyes open, but it's been quiet all season." Her attention is already moving to the next person in line, a farmhand with a basket of complaints.

Behind him, the mud-booted adventurer is still at the counter, unrolling the weasel pelt question backward — no, bargaining over where to buy a snare. The hearth pops. Rain has started outside, fine and hissing against the shutters.

The morning is his: Grainmarket Row to find the miller's yard, the rest of the board, or whatever else Redmarch holds until first light tomorrow.

VEYRHOLD [CANON + REGIONAL SEED]
Position: eastern Avereth. Capital: Ironward. Top-tier martial kingdom. Public S-ranks: 2.

Veyrhold is heavily militarized and shaped by dangerous borders. Martial training, disciplined officer corps, fortified cities and Monster-hunting traditions are central. Its most openly tense great-power relationship is with the Ashen Scale Dominion, though both avoid escalation into direct S-rank war.

GENERATION FLAVOR: fortification, logistics, readiness, veteran culture, border economies and social weight of service. Military presence should vary by location; civilians still trade, farm, marry, argue and live ordinary lives.
AVERETH — CANON AND GENERATIVE SPACE [AUTHORING RULE]
This lorebook is narrator/world knowledge, not knowledge any NPC automatically has. Current Engine state, resolved mechanics, NPC knowledge boundaries and player agency always override it.

Blank space is intentional. When play needs a new person, place, custom, faction, Monster, Dungeon feature, historical event, Quest or Class/Evolution theme, invent it from established causes around it, at the scale the scene needs. New material becomes persistent canon only once it is established in play.
AVERETH — WORLD IDENTITY [CANON]
The known world is dominated by one immense continent, Avereth, surrounded by ocean. Recorded history is extremely deep: civilizations, dynasties, religions and peoples have risen and vanished, and a few ancient beings remember eras ordinary people know only as legend.

The tone is high fantasy with contrast. Safe cities, farms, workshops, trade, families, festivals and ordinary careers coexist with dangerous wilderness, Monsters, natural Dungeons, political violence and ancient powers. The world is not uniformly grim and is not built as a sequence of combat zones.

Current established great powers are six human kingdoms — Valedorn Crown, Caelreth, Veyrhold, Solmere, Ilyrion and Duskreach — plus two recognized monster realms, the Ashen Scale Dominion and Verdant Fang Court. Human and monster states are not unified species blocs; trade, diplomacy, rivalry, war and cooperation can cross species lines.

Material culture is Western-fantasy medieval alongside mana and high magic. Modern or industrial technology is not the default.
blocks.b151:
"Herb Run as well." The clerk logs the second slip without ceremony. "Full basket, mind — a handful of sprigs won't pass. Reedbeds start past the mill leat, east side; follow the drainage path and you'll hear the marsh before you see it. Bring the basket back for weighing."

The walk out takes the better part of an hour. Grainmarket Row gives way to cart tracks, then to a raised drainage path of packed earth running beside the leat, where the millrace's spill churns pale and cold. The rain has thinned to mist. Reed hisses in the wind off the water, and the smell changes — mud, cut grass, something green and rotting underneath.

The beds open out where the leat slackens: black water veined with reeds, hummocks of tussock grass, thin sheets of standing water that reflect the grey sky. Marshmint shows itself easily enough once he knows to look — low stems with squared corners and dark leaves, growing in clumps at the waterline, some reachable from the path, others out on the hummocks where the footing will be mud to the shin. A heretofore unnoticed detail: something has beaten a flat trail through the reeds out toward open water, wide as a badger, the stems bent rather than cut.

A wading bird startles somewhere out in the beds and flaps away. Otherwise, only wind and water.

The basket problem is immediate — he carries none. The clumps nearest the path can be picked and carried in an armful, but a full basket will want a container from town or a good deal of trips.

blocks.b154:
The first armful is easy — clumps within reach of the path, stems snapping clean, mint smell sharp on his hands. He lays it on the dry boards of the drainage path and wades out for more.

The second and third armfuls cost wet boots. The hummock clumps grow out over black mud that takes each step to the shin and tries to keep the foot on the pull-back. By the fourth trip he has learned to read the tussocks — step on the grass mounds, not between them — and his pace improves. The rain holds at mist. Somewhere behind the reeds the leat keeps up its low constant chatter.

He works through the morning and into early afternoon, shuttling armfuls back to a growing pile on the path. The beaten trail in the reeds stays quiet each time he passes it; whatever made it has come and gone in the night, and the only fresh sign is a scatter of small tracks near the waterline — webbed, bird-sized.

By mid-afternoon the pile is respectable: a dense green heap the size of a meal sack, maybe more, maybe short of a full basket's worth — hard to judge without the basket. His back and forearms ache from bending, his clothes are mud to the knee, and the beds ahead have been picked over along the path's reach. The fuller clumps remaining lie out toward open water — near that flattened trail — or a good walk further down the drainage path, where the reedbeds widen past a bend.

The light is still good for two or three hours. Town is an hour back, and the Guild takes weigh-ins before dusk closes.

blocks.b157:
Hauling it means improvising. He strips off his outer shirt, lays it on the path, and rakes the pile onto it, bundling the corners into a rough sling that drips mint smell and mud. The load rides heavy against his chest, wet stems cold through the cloth, and the hour's walk back along the drainage path is slow — the aching forearms complain every few hundred paces, and twice he has to stop and shift the bundle to keep the bottom from spilling.

The leat's noise falls behind. Grainmarket Row takes him in with its late-afternoon traffic — carters, a woman arguing over a sack of onions, steam off a cookshop vent — and mud-tracked, shirtless in the drizzle, he draws a look or two and nothing more.

The Guildhall is warmer than the street. The same clerk glances up, takes in the bundle, and comes around the counter to weigh it on the trade scales by the hearth, cutting the sling open and stacking the mint in the pan while water drips onto the stone flags.

"Stems are clean, leaves whole." The needle settles. She adds a last handful. "That'll pass." She marks the Herb Run slip complete in her register. "Payout's yours — say the word at the desk and she'll count it out. And you're on the Miller's Run cart tomorrow, first light, Harrow's yard." She wipes her hands on a rag. "You'll want dry boots before then. That mud will give you a fever, and dead escorts don't get paid."

The hearth hisses. Out the window the light is going copper over the rooftops, and there is still the matter of the evening — food, boots, a basket for nothing, and whatever else Redmarch does after dark.
